name: Background Frequency Map
description: Maps frequency content of background regions
algorithm: Background Frequency Map — Frequency Domain Analyzer
mechanism:
This method creates frequency maps of video backgrounds for forensic deepfake detection:

1. **Background Segmentation**: Face/body regions are segmented and separated from the background using semantic segmentation. The background region is isolated for independent frequency analysis, avoiding frequency interference from the dynamically changing foreground.

2. **Spatial Frequency Mapping**: 2D FFT is computed over background regions in each frame, creating a spatial frequency map. Natural backgrounds exhibit stable frequency content dominated by scene-specific features (texture of walls, furniture patterns, foliage). The frequency map reveals the spectral signature of the background.

3. **Temporal Frequency Stability**: Background frequency maps across frames are compared. In authentic video with a stationary camera, background frequencies remain nearly constant. Deepfake generators may introduce frame-to-frame frequency artifacts in the background — subtle spectral flickering from imperfect temporal consistency in the generation process.

4. **Cross-Region Frequency Consistency**: Different background regions should show frequency characteristics consistent with a single imaging pipeline. GAN or diffusion-generated backgrounds may show frequency inconsistencies between spatial regions — different noise patterns, compression artifacts, or spectral energy distributions in different parts of the generated background.

5. **Frequency Anomaly Scoring**: The temporal variance of background frequency maps, cross-region frequency consistency, and deviation from expected spectral profiles are combined into a forensic score. Elevated scores indicate backgrounds that exhibit frequency characteristics inconsistent with natural video capture.
parameters:
Analysis type: frequency
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through background frequency map analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
